no biopsy or histopathologic confirmation of tumor subtype

decisive_items: a destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus, forming a large soft-tissue mass
response.rationale: R5 best matches the raw imaging phenotype: a destructive maxillary sinus mass with heterogeneous enhancement, fluid-fluid level, orbital invasion, and rapid enlargement, all favoring rhabdomyosarcoma. R3 shares the destructive sinus lesion and T2 hyperintensity but lacks the more specific malignant soft-tissue and hemorrhagic features. R4 is contradicted by the destructive mass and antibiotic failure. R2 shares rapid destructive growth but is less site- and age-typical than rhabdomyosarcoma.

rejected.why: Periorbital swelling and erythema are superficial and explained by secondary inflammation; the destructive sinus/orbital mass and failure to improve on antibiotics exclude cellulitis as the primary diagnosis.
Ewing sarcoma is much less common in the pediatric maxillary sinus/orbit and lacks the fluid-fluid level and heterogeneous enhancement pattern that are more characteristic of rhabdomyosarcoma.
